solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A bison developing little growth

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters of the words grow into a new form

explanation.surface: A bison grows up from a small calf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges the letters of A BISON.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a miniature tree, deliberately kept small by pruning: a little growth.

clue.text: A nimby's special interest, apparently

parts.note: a nimby is someone who objects to development 'not in my' own neighbourhood; the acronym names the plot of ground behind the house

explanation.surface: A local objector cares only about one thing.
explanation.walkthrough: NIMBY stands for 'Not In My Back Yard', said of people who oppose developments near their own homes; 'apparently' admits the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym literally spells out the garden ground behind a house as the protester's sole concern.

clue.text: What St Lawrence 21 is to ocean-going ships

definitions.text: What St Lawrence 21 is to ocean-going ships

parts.words: What St Lawrence 21 is to ocean-going ships
parts.note: the St Lawrence Seaway (21 across) is the canal system that lets big ships sail from the Atlantic to the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A question about Canadian shipping on the St Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies 'Seaway': the St Lawrence Seaway was built so that ocean-going ships could pass through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterway that ships can pass through is described by this adjective, the purpose of the Seaway.

clue.text: Broadcasts put on by the pretentious

definitions.meaning: a station broadcasts a programme, it puts it on air
affected manners, as in 'putting on ... and graces'

explanation.surface: Programmes staged by snobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means transmits on radio or TV; the noun means affected, superior manners.

clue.text: Musical and ballet, oddly, that can be avoided

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Perón

indicators.note: oddly takes the letters in the odd-numbered positions of the word ballet

explanation.surface: A night of musical and dance one could happily skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps letters 1, 3 and 5 of BALLET: B, L, E.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare positive form of 'inevitable': capable of being escaped or sidestepped.

clue.text: Attractive wall-covering gets damaged — receiving repair

indicators.note: damaged words are broken up, so the letters of the following phrase are reassembled

explanation.surface: A pretty wall-covering is damaged while being repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets damaged' rearranges all fifteen letters of RECEIVING REPAIR into the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This climbing plant is grown over house walls for its foliage, which turns a vivid red in autumn.

clue.text: To check on golf club he may do circuits of course

definitions.text: he may do circuits of course

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to test something is to check it
a driver is the golf club used for long tee shots

explanation.surface: Someone goes to inspect a golf club, then does laps of the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests golf but is a motor-racing circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed to try out cars runs laps of a track to assess their performance.

clue.text: Party's instruction to vote against?

definitions.meaning: split as a command, telling someone to be one who votes 'no'

explanation.surface: A political party's whip tells members to oppose a motion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words it is the order 'Be a No!'
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for a festive knees-up; split up it becomes the order to oppose.

clue.text: What proofreader does — some of them end spellbound!

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Proofreaders become so absorbed that some end up spellbound by the text.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader corrects text, removing errors from it: the formal verb for making such corrections.

clue.text: Tool seen as standard for plain speaking, presumably

definitions.meaning: from the idiom 'to call a ... a ...', meaning to speak bluntly

explanation.surface: An implement regarded as the benchmark of blunt talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden digging implement, and the word used as the yardstick in the idiom for frank speech.

clue.text: Container holding extra whitewash

indicators.note: holding means the container word keeps the other piece within it

parts.note: a cup is a container for drinks
over means in addition, extra, left over

explanation.surface: A tin containing spare whitewash paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whitewash' looks like paint, but means concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitewash is a concealment of wrongdoing, an attempt to hide the facts.

clue.text: A sphere that's subject to mutation

definitions.text: A sphere that's subject to mutation

indicators.note: mutation is change, so the letters of the two words are altered in order

explanation.surface: A ball being changed in form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to mutation' rearranges A SPHERE; the whole clue also describes what happens to the sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a new form is what mutating a sphere does to it.

clue.text: I travel around with unknown Indian mystic

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

indicators.note: around signals that the pair I and travel are turned back to front

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Someone describes touring with a mysterious Indian holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses I GO to OGI, placed after Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A yogi is a practitioner of yoga, a Hindu ascetic or spiritual teacher from India.

clue.text: Died down or became a man of mystery

indicators.note: became means the letters turn into something else, a rearrangement of the three words

explanation.surface: Something either faded or turned into an enigmatic figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became' rearranges DIED DOWN OR. Dickens's unfinished novel is 'The Mystery of Edwin Drood', so its title character is literally a man of mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: The title figure of Dickens's last, unfinished novel, whose disappearance is never solved.

clue.text: Carpet-pile woven to portray the Cutty Sark,say

indicators.note: woven threads are interlaced, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rug woven with a picture of a famous ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges CARPET-PILE. The Cutty Sark is a preserved 19th-century sailing ship at Greenwich, London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cutty Sark is an example of a fast sailing ship built to carry tea from China.

clue.text: Polish that is given to stones, primarily, like these?

definitions.text: Polish that is given to stones, primarily, like these?

parts.note: to rub is to polish
i.e. abbreviates id est, 'that is'

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word stones is used

explanation.surface: Gems such as these receive polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is not Polish nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Red gemstones are typical of stones that are polished to bring out their lustre.

clue.text: Endless account with debts make you bad-tempered

indicators.note: Endless means the last letter of the word for account is dropped

parts.note: a bill is an account of what is owed
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: An unending bill plus a pile of debts would make anyone irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish and irritable; bile was once thought to cause bad temper.

clue.text: Not carried away, we're told, as children's presents quickly are

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: rapt means carried away, enthralled, so not rapt

explanation.surface: Restrained excitement compared to children tearing open gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Children open gifts hurriedly, so their packaging is quickly removed.

clue.text: Article from Hatter's Castle in Scotland

definitions.meaning: a hatter makes and sells headwear; one item is a flat Scottish bonnet
the royal family's residence on Deeside, Aberdeenshire

explanation.surface: Something taken from the novel Hatter's Castle, set in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hatter's Castle' is A. J. Cronin's novel, but the words split into two senses: a hatter's article and a Scottish castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimless Scottish bonnet, and the Highland royal estate it was named after.

clue.text: Busy ports mostly work spasmodically

indicators.note: work means the letters are worked into a fresh order
mostly means not all of the word ports is used: one letter goes

explanation.surface: Busy harbours mostly operate in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the O of PORTS, and 'work' rearranges BUSY PRTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in short bursts of effort is working fitfully, in irregular spells.

clue.text: Old soldier and deserter caught breaking code

indicators.note: caught means the deserter word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a rat is one who deserts, like a rat leaving a sinking ship

indicators.note: breaking means the word code is broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A deserter is arrested while cracking a cipher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' looks like cracking a cipher but scrambles the word into EDCO; 'caught' is the containment signal, not an arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoats were British soldiers of the past, named for their scarlet tunics.

clue.text: Main road, you might say

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a way is a road, as in a highway

explanation.surface: A description of a chief highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like 'principal' but is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel for ships is a road across the water, a route on the main.

clue.text: One degree Celsius on US counting device

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the preceding pieces sit above US

parts.note: a is one, the indefinite article
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A temperature reading of one degree, recorded on an American gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degree' looks like a temperature unit beside Celsius, but is a university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads on rods used for arithmetic, the oldest calculating tool.

clue.text: Strike or 26

definitions.meaning: 26 across means to find fault, and this word can mean to criticise

explanation.surface: A cross-reference offering a choice of hitting or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to hit and, informally, to disparage or criticise.

clue.text: Think about 12, maybe

definitions.meaning: to keep something in your thoughts
12 across is a name shared by the cartoon bear Yogi, so thinking of one is having an animal on one's mind

explanation.surface: A prompt to consider the Indian mystic.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 across is YOGI; Yogi Bear is the cartoon character, so thinking of him puts a bear in your mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to remember or consider something; literally, a bear held in one's thoughts.

clue.text: The island needs what travellers often pay

definitions.meaning: a ring-shaped coral reef enclosing a lagoon
split in two, a charge levied on a bridge or road

explanation.surface: Visiting the island costs travellers a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A TOLL, a fee paid to use a road or bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A coral reef island ringing a lagoon; read as two words, a road or bridge fee.

clue.text: Find fault with the fish

definitions.meaning: a freshwater fish common in ponds

explanation.surface: Criticising someone's fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to complain pettily; the noun is a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Four points given for intelligence

definitions.meaning: the four compass points, north, east, west and south, abbreviated
intelligence in the sense of information or reports

explanation.surface: Scoring four points in exchange for information.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intelligence' means information, not cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence here means information received, reports of recent events.

clue.text: Aircraft commonly of metal gets hot inside

indicators.note: inside means the letter for hot is placed within the metal word

parts.note: copper is a metal
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An aircraft made of metal gets hot within.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial name for a helicopter, so 'commonly' marks the informal register.

clue.text: See 5
Wee fellow in Ulster resolved to give up time to independence

indicators.note: in means the small being is placed inside the other letters
resolved suggests the remaining letters are sorted into a new order
to give up means that letter is taken out of Ulster

parts.note: an elf is a small mythical being

explanation.surface: A little man in Northern Ireland determines to sacrifice time for freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is Northern Ireland. 'to give up' removes T, and 'resolved' rearranges the remaining ULSER into S + RULE, with 'in' setting the small being between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-government, a state or people ruling itself, is political independence.

clue.text: A team's words not for everyone to hear

definitions.text: words not for everyone to hear

parts.note: a side is a team, and 's adds the S

explanation.surface: A team's private remarks among themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks muttered so only some can hear, like an actor's stage remarks to the audience.
